# Could muscle hold up a tree?

<!-- STEP id="imagine-muscle" -->
## An imagined test

This is only an imagined test. Suppose the neem tree had no cell walls, and muscle like the muscle in a rabbit's leg had to hold it upright.

<!-- STEP id="muscle-uses-energy" -->
## Muscle holds only while it uses energy

Hold a full school bag out in front of you with a straight arm. Your arm muscle stays tight only while it keeps using energy, so after a minute or two your arm gets tired and drops. To hold up a tree, muscle would have to keep using energy day and night.

<!-- STEP id="wall-uses-none" -->
## A wall holds without working

A cell wall is different. Once it is made, it stays stiff and keeps its shape without using any energy.

**For a body that stands in one place for many years, stiff cell walls are a far better support than muscle.**

image.alt: A rabbit's leg muscle in close-up, and an imagined tree held up by red ropes of muscle that sag, with a red cross.
